gaps.sentence: So convincing ___ her argument that even the sceptics agreed.
gaps.explanation: 'So convincing was her argument that …' — 'so + adj' fronted with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Only in an emergency ___ this exit be used.
gaps.explanation: may + be + participle: this exit may be used only in an emergency.

gaps.sentence: Not until every passenger had been evacuated ___ the captain leave the ship.
gaps.explanation: 'Not until … did the captain leave …' — inverted past simple.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets expensive, but they were also sold out.
gaps.explanation: Not only were the tickets… — inversion with 'be' needs no auxiliary.

gaps.sentence: Not until the film ended ___ anybody speak.
gaps.explanation: Not until + time clause at the front: did anybody speak.

gaps.sentence: To such an extent ___ prices risen that buyers withdrew.
gaps.hint: To such an extent + past perfect
gaps.explanation: To such an extent had prices risen that… — emphatic result.

gaps.sentence: ___ the second half begin than the rain returned.
gaps.explanation: No sooner did the second half begin than… — inversion with do-support.

gaps.sentence: Not since the winter of 1963 ___ temperatures dropped so low.
gaps.explanation: 'Not since 1963 have temperatures dropped …' — the only time from then until now.
